notes: Verbatim import (Stage 73). Each RFC hex-dump field (byte-offset column + space-separated hex bytes + ASCII-annotation column, or colon-separated tag bytes) has been concatenated into a single lowercase hex string per field — this is a minimal, non-value-altering formatting change (offsets/ASCII annotations/colons/'0x' prefixes are formatting, not vector data). No byte value was added, removed, or reordered; the plaintext fields were cross-checked by decoding the extracted hex as UTF-8/ASCII and comparing byte-for-byte against the RFC's own printed plaintext text. RFC 8439 does not itself publish byte-level tamper/negative vectors (bit-flipped tag/ciphertext/AAD) for this construction — per the verbatim-only, no-independent-generation rule (docs/crypto_test_vectors.md §3, docs/crypto_vector_sources.md §2), no such negative vector is fabricated here. Negative/tamper cases for this primitive remain a future, explicitly-labeled 'generated' Stage, not part of this import. No Rust code reads this file yet.

vectors.plaintextUtf8: Ladies and Gentlemen of the class of '99: If I could offer you only one tip for the future, sunscreen would be it.
vectors.notes: nonce = nonceConstant (32-bit fixed-common part, sender id=7) || nonceIv (64-bit IV), per RFC 8439 §2.8.2's own construction of the 96-bit AEAD nonce. The RFC's 'AEAD Construction for Poly1305' buffer (AAD || padding || ciphertext || padding || lengths) is used internally to compute the tag; it is not itself an output field and is not duplicated here.

vectors.description: RFC 8439 Appendix A.5 full ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD decryption worked example (the 'Internet-Drafts' plaintext); the RFC computes the tag and confirms it equals the received tag before decrypting.
vectors.plaintextUtf8: Internet-Drafts are draft documents valid for a maximum of six months and may be updated, replaced, or obsoleted by other documents at any time. It is inappropriate to use Internet-Drafts as reference material or to cite them other than as /“work in progress./”
vectors.notes: The RFC's 'Received Tag' and independently 'Calculated Tag' are identical in the source text (the worked example demonstrates a matching tag before decrypting); both are recorded as receivedTag/calculatedTag for traceability, and 'tag' duplicates the same value as the field a test harness would compare against.
